subject.title: improve: index transcript mirror persistence checks

question: Should OpenClaw expose these three generic transcript write-lock fact methods as a durable Plugin SDK contract, or should the performance work remain owner-specific until a broader SDK API is approved?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow, but it extends a compatibility-sensitive public plugin surface whose permanent semantics cannot be selected safely by automated review.

options.title: Approve the narrow SDK contract
options.body: Accept the three methods as public write-lock facts, then merge the parent, rebase this PR, and validate the exact head before landing.

options.title: Keep the optimization owner-specific
options.body: Replace the public generic methods with a narrower internal or owner-injected seam if maintainers do not want external plugins to depend on these persistence facts.

options.title: Pause the child with the parent
options.body: Defer both stacked changes until maintainers choose the desired transcript SDK and migration direction together.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow SDK contract
recommendation.body: Accept the three methods as public write-lock facts, then merge the parent, rebase this PR, and validate the exact head before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked generation foundation and this dependent consumer implementation, so they can explain the intended contract and alternatives.
